nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the ballot number $B(n, n)$ equals the $n$-th Catalan number $C_n$.
nodes.title: Diagonal ballot numbers are Catalan numbers

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the ballot number $B(n, 0)$ equals $1$.
nodes.title: Ballot numbers with second index zero

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$, the ballot number $B(n, k)$ is the integer part of $\max(n + 1 - k, 0) \binom{n+k}{n} / (n + 1)$. For $k \le n + 1$ the division is exact, so $B(n, k) = \frac{n - k + 1}{n + 1} \binom{n+k}{n}$ (OEIS A009766), and $B(n, k) = 0$ for $k > n + 1$.
nodes.title: Ballot numbers

nodes.summary: Let $p \ge 1$ and let $(d, r)$ be a smooth arithmetical structure on the coconut tree $CT(p, 2)$, whose path is $v_1, \dots, v_p$ and whose two leaves are attached to the central vertex $v_p$. Then $d(v_p) \le 1$.
nodes.title: Smooth structures on coconut trees with two leaves

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a pair of vertex labelings $(d, r)$ of the coconut tree $CT(p, s)$ and $y$ a pair of vertex labelings of $CT(q, t)$. Then $y$ is an ancestor of $x$, and $x$ a descendant of $y$, when $y$ is obtained from $x$ by a finite, possibly empty, sequence of smoothings, each performed at a vertex where the current $d$-label equals $1$: either at a path vertex other than the central vertex, or at a leaf.
nodes.title: Ancestors of labelings of coconut trees

nodes.summary: For every natural number $x$, the term $A(x, 0)$ of the coconut tree count equals the Catalan number $C_{x-1}$, read as $C_0$ when $x = 0$.
nodes.title: The coconut count term with second argument zero

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $x$ and $y$, the term $A(x, y)$ is defined by $A(x, 0) = C_{x-1}$, $A(x, 1) = C_{x-1} - C_{x-2}$ and, for $y \ge 2$,
nodes.title: Terms of the coconut tree count

nodes.summary: Let $p$ and $s$ be natural numbers with $p + s \ge 2$, let $(d, r)$ be an arithmetical structure on the coconut tree $CT(p, s + 1)$, and let $\ell$ be a leaf with $d(\ell) = 1$. Then the labelings $(d', r')$ obtained by smoothing $(d, r)$ at $\ell$ form an arithmetical structure on $CT(p, s)$.
nodes.title: Smoothing a leaf preserves arithmetical structures

nodes.summary: On the coconut tree $CT(4, 4)$, write a labeling as (values at $v_1, \dots, v_4$ | values at the leaves $\ell_1, \dots, \ell_4$). Take $d = (1, 3, 2, 3 \mid 2, 2, 3, 1)$ and $r = (2, 2, 4, 6 \mid 3, 3, 2, 6)$. Smoothing at the path vertex $v_1$ and then at the leaf $\ell_4$ gives the labelings $d' = (2, 2, 2 \mid 2, 2, 3)$ and $r' = (2, 4, 6 \mid 3, 3, 2)$ on $CT(3, 3)$.
nodes.title: An example of smoothing at a path vertex and at a leaf

nodes.summary: Let the coconut tree $CT(p, s + 1)$ have path vertices $v_1, \dots, v_p$, central vertex $v_p$ and leaves $\ell_1, \dots, \ell_{s+1}$, let $d$ and $r$ be labelings of its vertices by natural numbers, and let $1 \le k \le s + 1$. Smoothing $(d, r)$ at the leaf $\ell_k$ gives the labelings $(d', r')$ of $CT(p, s)$ obtained by deleting $\ell_k$ and renumbering the remaining leaves…
nodes.title: Smoothing at a leaf of a coconut tree

nodes.summary: Let $s \ge 1$ and let $(d, r)$ be an arithmetical structure on the coconut tree $CT(p + 1, s)$, whose path vertices are $v_1, \dots, v_{p+1}$ with central vertex $v_{p+1}$. If $d(v_k) = 1$ for some non-central path vertex $v_k$ (that is, $1 \le k \le p$), then smoothing $(d, r)$ at $v_k$ gives an arithmetical structure on $CT(p, s)$.
nodes.title: Path smoothing preserves arithmetical structures on coconut trees

nodes.summary: List a labeling of a coconut tree as its values on the path vertices $v_1, v_2, \dots$, then $\mid$, then its values on the leaves. Smoothing the labelings $d = (3, 1, 3, 2, 2 \mid 2, 2, 4)$ and $r = (1, 3, 2, 3, 4 \mid 2, 2, 1)$ of $CT(5, 3)$ at $v_2$ gives the labelings $d' = (2, 2, 2, 2 \mid 2, 2, 4)$ and $r' = (1, 2, 3, 4 \mid 2, 2, 1)$ of $CT(4, 3)$.
nodes.title: Example of smoothing a coconut tree at a path vertex

nodes.summary: Let the coconut tree $CT(p + 1, s)$ have path vertices $v_1, \dots, v_{p+1}$, central vertex $v_{p+1}$ and leaves $\ell_1, \dots, \ell_s$, let $d$ and $r$ be labelings of its vertices by natural numbers, and let $1 \le k \le p + 1$. Smoothing $(d, r)$ at $v_k$ gives the labelings $(d', r')$ of $CT(p, s)$ obtained by deleting $v_k$ and renumbering the remaining path vertices…
nodes.title: Smoothing at a path vertex of a coconut tree

nodes.summary: If $(d, r)$ is an arithmetical structure on the coconut tree $CT(p, s)$, whose path vertices are $v_1, \dots, v_p$, then for every $1 \le k \le p$, subdividing $(d, r)$ at position $k$ (inserting a new path vertex just before $v_k$) gives an arithmetical structure on $CT(p + 1, s)$.
nodes.title: Subdivision preserves arithmetical structures on coconut trees

nodes.summary: List a labeling of a coconut tree as its values on the path vertices $v_1, v_2, \dots$, then $\mid$, then its values on the leaves. Subdividing the labelings $d = (2, 2, 2, 2 \mid 2, 2, 4)$ and $r = (1, 2, 3, 4 \mid 2, 2, 1)$ of $CT(4, 3)$ at position $2$ gives the labelings $d' = (3, 1, 3, 2, 2 \mid 2, 2, 4)$ and $r' = (1, 3, 2, 3, 4 \mid 2, 2, 1)$ of $CT(5, 3)$. These are the labelings of Example 3.2, whose…
nodes.title: Example of subdividing a coconut tree

nodes.summary: Let the coconut tree $CT(p, s)$ have path vertices $v_1, \dots, v_p$ and leaves $\ell_1, \dots, \ell_s$, let $d$ and $r$ be labelings of its vertices by natural numbers, and let $1 \le k \le p$. Subdividing $(d, r)$ at position $k$ gives the labelings $(d', r')$ of $CT(p + 1, s)$ obtained by inserting a new path vertex $w$ just before $v_k$, so that the path becomes $v_1, \dots, v_{k-1}, w, v_k, \dots, v_p$, with…
nodes.title: Subdivision at a path vertex of a coconut tree

nodes.summary: Let $(d, r)$ be an arithmetical structure on the coconut tree $CT(p, s)$ with path vertices $v_1, \dots, v_p$, and write $d_k = d(v_k)$ and $r_k = r(v_k)$. The following are equivalent: (1) $d_k \ge 2$ for $1 \le k \le p - 1$; (2) $0 < r_2 - r_1 \le r_3 - r_2 \le \cdots \le r_p - r_{p-1}$; (3) $r_1 < r_2 < \cdots < r_p$.
nodes.title: Monotonicity criteria for arithmetical structures on coconut trees

nodes.summary: Let the coconut tree $CT(p, s)$ have path vertices $v_1, \dots, v_p$. Two path vertices $v_a$ and $v_b$ are adjacent if and only if $|a - b| = 1$.
nodes.title: Adjacent path vertices of a coconut tree

nodes.summary: Let the coconut tree $CT(p, s)$ have path vertices $v_1, \dots, v_p$, with central vertex $v_p$. A leaf of $CT(p, s)$ is adjacent to a path vertex $v_k$ if and only if $k = p$.
nodes.title: Adjacency of leaves and path vertices in a coconut tree

nodes.summary: No leaf of the coconut tree $CT(p, s)$ is adjacent to a leaf.
nodes.title: Leaves of a coconut tree are pairwise nonadjacent

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $p$ and $s$, the coconut tree $\mathrm{CT}(p, s)$ is the graph whose vertices are the path vertices $v_1, \dots, v_p$ and the leaves $v_{\ell_1}, \dots, v_{\ell_s}$, in which $v_i$ and $v_{i+1}$ are adjacent for $1 \le i < p$, every leaf is adjacent to $v_p$, and there are no other edges. For $p = 0$ it consists of $s$ isolated vertices.
nodes.title: Coconut tree

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be the Euclidean chain function, let $p \ge 1$, and let $(d, r)$ be a smooth arithmetical structure on the coconut tree $\mathrm{CT}(p, s)$, with path vertices $v_1, \dots, v_p$ and leaves $v_{\ell_1}, \dots, v_{\ell_s}$. Then $p = F(r(v_{\ell_1}) + \dots + r(v_{\ell_s}), r(v_p)) - 1$.
nodes.title: Path length of a smooth arithmetical structure on a coconut tree

nodes.summary: Let $(d, r)$ be a smooth arithmetical structure on the coconut tree $\mathrm{CT}(p, s)$ with leaves $v_{\ell_1}, \dots, v_{\ell_s}$. If a natural number $g$ divides $r(v_{\ell_j})$ for every $j = 1, \dots, s$, then $g = 1$.
nodes.title: The leaf labels of a smooth arithmetical structure on a coconut tree are coprime

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $x \ge 1$, $y$ and $k$, the Euclidean chain function $F$ satisfies $F(x + k y, y) = F(x, y)$ and $F(x, k x + y) = F(x, y) + k$.
nodes.title: Euclidean chain function under adding multiples

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $x, y \ge 1$ with $x \mid y$, the Euclidean chain function $F$ satisfies $F(x, y) = 1 + y / x$.
nodes.title: Euclidean chain function when the first argument divides the second

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $x$ and $y$ with $y \ne 0$, the Euclidean chain function $F$ satisfies $F(x, y) = 1 + F(y, (-x) \bmod y)$, where $(-x) \bmod y$ is the least nonnegative residue of $-x$ modulo $y$.
nodes.title: Recursion for the Euclidean chain function

nodes.summary: For every natural number $y$, the Euclidean chain function $F$ satisfies $F(1, y) = y + 1$, and for every natural number $x \ge 1$ it satisfies $F(x, 1) = 2$.
nodes.title: Euclidean chain function at one

nodes.summary: The Euclidean chain function $F$ satisfies $F(13, 60) = 8$.
nodes.title: Euclidean chain function of 13 and 60

nodes.summary: For every natural number $x$, the Euclidean chain function $F$ satisfies $F(x, 0) = 1$.
nodes.title: Euclidean chain function with second argument zero

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $x_1$ and $x_2$, the Euclidean chain $x_1, x_2, x_3, \dots$ is given by $x_{i+1} = (-x_{i-1}) \bmod x_i$ (the least nonnegative residue) while $x_i \ne 0$, and by $x_{i+1} = 0$ once $x_i = 0$. The Euclidean chain function is defined by the recursion $F(x, 0) = 1$ and $F(x, y) = 1 + F(y, (-x) \bmod y)$ for $y \ne 0$. For $x_1 > 0$, $F(x_1, x_2)$ is the number of positive terms of the Euclidean…
nodes.title: Euclidean chain function

nodes.summary: Let $s \ge 1$ and let $c$ and $a_1, \dots, a_s$ be natural numbers with $a_i > 0$, $a_i \mid c$ and $a_i < c$ for every $i$, such that the only natural number dividing $c$ and all of $a_1, \dots, a_s$ is $1$. Write $CT(p, s)$ for the coconut tree with path vertices $v_1, \dots, v_p$ and leaves $\ell_1, \dots, \ell_s$ adjacent to $v_p$. Then there is exactly one $p \ge 1$ such that $CT(p, s)$ carries a smooth…
nodes.title: Smooth coconut structures with prescribed labels

nodes.summary: Let $s \ge 1$ and let $(d, r)$ be an arithmetical structure on the coconut tree $CT(p, s)$ with $d(\ell_j) \ge 2$ at every leaf $\ell_j$. Then there is exactly one pair consisting of a number $q$ with $1 \le q \le p$ and a smooth arithmetical structure on $CT(q, s)$ that is a coconut ancestor of $(d, r)$, that is, one obtained from $(d, r)$ by a possibly empty sequence of smoothings, each performed at a vertex…
nodes.title: Unique smooth ancestor

nodes.summary: On the graph with two vertices joined by an edge, the labelings $d = (1, 1)$ and $r = (1, 1)$ form an arithmetical structure.
nodes.title: The all-ones structure on a single edge

nodes.summary: An arithmetical structure on a graph $G$ with vertex set $V$ is a pair of labelings $d, r : V \to \mathbb{N}$ such that $d(v) > 0$ and $r(v) > 0$ for every vertex $v$, $d(v)\, r(v) = \sum_{w \sim v} r(w)$ for every vertex $v$, where the sum runs over the neighbours $w$ of $v$, and the only natural number dividing every $r(v)$ is $1$. For a finite graph with adjacency matrix $A$ the middle condition reads…
nodes.title: Arithmetical structure

nodes.summary: Let $p \ge 1$ and let $(d, r)$ be an arithmetical structure on the coconut tree $CT(p, s)$ with path vertices $v_1, \dots, v_p$ and leaves $\ell_1, \dots, \ell_s$ adjacent to $v_p$. Then $(d, r)$ is smooth if and only if $r(\ell_j) < r(v_p)$ for every $j$ and $r(v_1) < r(v_2) < \dots < r(v_p)$.
nodes.title: Characterization of smooth coconut structures

nodes.summary: Let $CT(p, s)$ be the coconut tree with path vertices $v_1, \dots, v_p$ and leaves $\ell_1, \dots, \ell_s$ adjacent to $v_p$. An arithmetical structure $(d, r)$ on $CT(p, s)$ is smooth if $d(v_i) \ge 2$ for $1 \le i \le p - 1$ and $d(\ell_j) \ge 2$ for $1 \le j \le s$; there is no condition on $d(v_p)$.
nodes.title: Smooth arithmetical structure on a coconut tree

nodes.title: Counting coconut structures whose leaves cannot be smoothed

nodes.summary: For every integer $p \ge 1$, the number of arithmetical structures $(d, r)$ on the coconut tree $\mathrm{CT}(p, 1)$, which is the path on $p + 1$ vertices, whose leaf $\ell_1$ has $d_{\ell_1} \ne 1$ (so that the leaf cannot be smoothed) is $C_p - C_{p-1}$, where $C_n$ denotes the $n$-th Catalan number.
nodes.title: Arithmetical structures on a one-leaf coconut tree with a non-smoothable leaf

nodes.summary: Let $s \ge 2$ and $1 \le i \le p$, and let $(d, r)$ be a smooth arithmetical structure on the coconut tree $\mathrm{CT}(i, s)$. Then exactly $B(p - 1, p - i)$ arithmetical structures on $\mathrm{CT}(p, s)$ are descendants of $(d, r)$, where $B(n, k)$ is the ballot number.
nodes.title: Number of descendants of a smooth coconut structure

nodes.summary: Let $p \ge 1$ and let $(d, r)$ be a smooth arithmetical structure on the coconut tree $\mathrm{CT}(p, s)$, with central vertex $v_p$ and leaves $\ell_1, \ldots, \ell_s$. Then $d_{v_p} > 1$ if and only if $r_{v_p} < \sum_{j=1}^{s} r_{\ell_j}$.
nodes.title: Smooth coconut structures with central label above one

nodes.summary: If $(d, r)$ is a smooth arithmetical structure on the coconut tree $\mathrm{CT}(p, s)$, then $d_{\ell_j} \ge 2$ for every leaf $\ell_j$, $1 \le j \le s$.
nodes.title: Leaves of a smooth coconut structure have label at least 2

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
